kind: a gravity irrigation canal and the farms along it
one_line: One canal, its turns taken in a fixed order, and a court that sits on Thursdays and writes nothing down.
monitor_rationale: logs headgate openings and closings; four months, then we look again

ladder.label: turn-order
ladder.text: Water is taken in the order of the ditch, head to tail, and a turn missed is a turn waited for.

shared.label: canal-works
shared.text: Work on the canal itself is agreed before it is paid for out of the common fund.

access.label: land-carries-water
access.text: The right to water belongs to the land, and passes with it.

inner_a.label: gate-by-rider
inner_a.text: The headgate is opened and shut by a ditch-rider, never by the farm taking the water.

inner_b.label: gate-logged
inner_b.text: Every opening of the headgate is called out and logged the same day.

clash_a.label: no-storage
clash_a.text: Water is taken to the field, not held in a private pond.

clash_b.label: night-turns-stored
clash_b.text: A turn that falls at night may be held until morning rather than run onto a dark field.

extra.label: gate-marks
extra.text: A headgate carries the mark of the farm it serves.

policy.root: We decide by consent: one reasoned objection stops a thing, and saying nothing is not an objection. Changing an ordinance takes the assembly, and anything that cannot be undone is not decided by silence.
policy.inner: Whoever the canal elected as ditch-riders decides the headgate.
policy.unheld: The wellfield is decided by whoever holds it.
policy.ladder: The first time the canal asks. The second time the assembly asks together. The third time the answer is no.
policy.inner_amended: Two of us have to object before a headgate decision stops.

inner_proposal.text: let a farm open its own headgate when the rider is at the far end
inner_proposal.because: a turn lost waiting for the rider is water down the tail of the canal

inner_objection: the rider at the gate is the whole reason nobody argues about how long a turn ran

unheld_proposal.text: sink two more wells to carry the canal through August

monitor_watch.about: a gate open out of turn at first light
monitor_watch.because: the gate was opened before the turn above it had closed
monitor_watch.dismissal: these two do not really conflict

ladder_subject.first: take an hour ahead of turn while the tail is still running
ladder_subject.second: take another hour ahead of turn for the same field
ladder_subject.third: take the whole turn a day early through the dry week
ladder_subject.because: an hour taken early is an hour the farm below waited for and did not get
ladder_subject.ruling_1: the seedbed was going and we let it stand
ladder_subject.ruling_2: the assembly agreed one more, then no more

other_subject.text: widen the field ditch so the turn runs off faster

clash.about: holding a night turn until morning
clash.text: let the three tail farms hold a night turn in the old pond and run it at first light
clash.because_a: water held in a private pond is water the canal cannot see and cannot count
clash.because_b: a night turn run onto a dark field is a turn spent on the road and the ditch bank
clash.carried: the pond is on the tail where nothing runs below it, and the alternative is three farms taking their turns twice; revisit when the night gate is automated

amend_convention.text: number the gates instead of marking them with the farm
amend_convention.because: farms change hands and the marks have not been repainted in years

amend_principle.text: allow a pond on any farm below the last gate
amend_principle.because: nothing runs below the last gate, so nothing there can be taken from anybody

irreversible.text: break out the old brick channel and line the whole run in concrete

silence.about: who clears the grating after a storm
silence.rationale: whoever is nearest has always gone, and a duty would make it late rather than immediate
silence.proposal: set a rota for clearing the grating

panel.rationale: three of us to look at the night-turn rule for a month
